title: Control Plane Procurement, CTO/Ops Q&A and Competitive Notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working doc for AEs/SEs + PMs to prep for procurement/CTO/Platform engineering conversations on customer-managed control planes (VPC/on-prem). Focus: expected asks, concise language choices, likely objections and pithy rebuttals, and competitive deltas to have in memory during early procurement.

Status: rough; pull quotes and snippets into AE playbook. Not customer-facing as-is.

Audience:
- CTO/Head of Platform (primary)
- Infrastructure/Platform Eng leads
- Security & Compliance contacts (CISO/delegates)
- Procurement/Legal for contract asks

Topline positioning (3 lines):
- We separate control plane metadata from customer data: control plane can be customer-hosted in their VPC or run in Redwood-managed region with strict telemetry controls.
- We provide a simple switch: fully customer-managed control plane (VPC peered or private link) or hybrid managed; same API surface and tooling across both.
- Decision criteria for customers: regulatory boundary (data residency/air-gap), operational ownership, and procurement friction (SLA + support model).

Language choices (why words matter):
- Avoid: "air-gapped install" (scary/legal triggers). Use "isolated deployment option (on-prem)".
- Use: "customer-managed control plane" or "VPC-hosted control plane" when buyer needs ownership/visibility.
- Use: "data plane remains in customer network" vs "control plane handles metadata only". Emphasize that inference data processing happens where they choose.

Common buyer objections + concise rebuttals (talk-track bullets):
- "We can't trust an external control plane with metadata."
  - Rebuttal: "You can opt for customer-managed control plane in your VPC. We provide an installable control-plane image and runbook; audit logs map every action to your identity provider."
- "On-prem is too slow/expensive to manage."
  - Rebuttal: "Redwood supports hybrid: control plane in your VPC + optional hosted fallbacks for burst capacity under contract. We provide autoscaling policies so ops overhead is minimized."
- "We need KMS/HSM and key custody guarantees."
  - Rebuttal: "Integrates with your KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault), and we provide documented key rotation & audit flows. Sample contract language included in linked_artifacts."
- "What about upgrades and security patches?"
  - Rebuttal: "Lifecycle options: you can accept managed upgrades (we push within maintenance windows) or run our curated upgrade artifacts and follow our documented SRE playbook. We offer optional upgrade services for enterprise contracts."

Procurement & contract asks to expect (operational checklist):
- Data residency and sovereignty clause (explicit: inference data never leaves customer VPC without opt-in).
- Support & SLA spec: control-plane uptime (if Redwood-managed), RTO for incident response, and priority support hours.
- Liability/cap on data leakage — standard enterprise redlines; prepare fallback language: shared responsibility model doc.
- Compliance attachments: SOC2 type II, ISO, penetration test reports (redacted), and on-prem installation attestations.

Competitive deltas (short bullets to memorize):
- Competitor A (big cloud vendor endpoints):
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration, single-vendor stack for customers on that cloud.
  - Redwood delta: Neutral control-plane story (we run in any cloud or on-prem), consistent developer API across hosted/dedicated/private — easier multi-cloud or hybrid migrations.
- Competitor B (self-hosted inference vendor):
  - Strengths: full on-prem control, mature ops tooling for some customers.
  - Redwood delta: Better opinionated runtime optimizations out-of-the-box (KV caching, batching heuristics) + managed rollouts & eval hooks; lower engineering lift for equivalent throughput.
- Competitor C (LLM API provider with 'private instances'):
  - Strengths: simple procurement, packaged offering.
  - Redwood delta: Clear separation of control vs data plane and stronger compliance artefacts for regulated industries; explicit KMS/HSM and private network options.

Technical Q&A (short answers for SEs):
- Q: "Does control plane see model prompts or outputs?"
  - A: "By default only metadata (request ids, routing decisions). If customer chooses managed routing with logging enabled, there is an opt-in telemetry mode — otherwise inference payloads remain in the customer data plane."
- Q: "How do we handle KV cache persistence across restarts?"
  - A: "Local NVMe-backed cache with optional export to customer-managed S3 compliant storage for warm start; documented TTLs and eviction policies in the runbook."
- Q: "What network topologies do we support?"
  - A: "VPC peering, PrivateLink, Site-to-site VPN, and on-prem air-gapped deployment using an offline installer + attestations. Recommend PrivateLink for low-latency secure control plane endpoints."
- Q: "Can we restrict model versions available to tenants?"
  - A: "Yes — policy engine can pin model version per tenant, per route, or global. We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies in case of regressions."

Sales/Rollout snippets (for AE/SE):
- Opening line for CTO: "We help you keep inference inside your boundaries while giving product teams a cloud-like API. Two deployment choices: full customer-managed control plane or hybrid with strict telemetry controls — both keep developer UX consistent."
- Procurement nudge: "We typically deliver an SOC2 packet + an installation attestation within 7 business days once the SOW is signed. If you need HSM integration, we add the KMS appendix to the contract."

Sample email (short) to CTO/Platform lead:
- Subject: "Demo + control-plane deployment options for [Company] — low-friction on-prem"
- Body: "Hi <Name>,
We'd like to show a short demo of Redwood's VPC-hosted control plane and the installer for on-prem. We'll also bring a sample SOW and our support/SLA matrix so procurement can parallelize. Is Thurs 10–11am OK?
Thanks,
Aisha (cc: SE team)"

Open questions / risky asks to triage with Eng/Legal: (TODOs)
- What is the minimum support window for on-prem upgrades included in enterprise plans? (Ask Eng: recommended cadence + compatibility matrix.)
- Clarify telemetry/data plane logs: provide template for 'no-persistent-logging' clause. (Legal to draft.)
- Pricing: how do we price dedicated on-prem installs vs VPC-hosted control plane? (Finance input needed.)

Next steps (owners):
- Priya: draft KMS integration appendix (due 2026-02-22).
- Luca: build short slide for AE playbook with 3 screenshots + 2 talking bullets (due 2026-02-10).
- Marco: confirm offline installer MD5 signing approach with infra (due 2026-02-18).
- Aisha: consolidate legal redlines template and circulate to go-to-market (due 2026-02-20).

Notes to self / rough bits:
- Keep a small one-pager "control plane explainer" with diagram: customer VPC (data plane) <-> control plane (metadata) — emphasize no payload storage by default.
- Link to existing install-runbook (CONF-PL-3245) and bump with quickstart for procurement checklist.
- Keep rebuttals short (1–2 lines) for SEs — long form in confluence only.

End of doc.
